cases.reason: Baltimore's head coach said on August 31 that the Week 1 center job remains a real competition between Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic. A one-for-one replacement is therefore not yet established.
cases.reopenTrigger: Official/reliable Week 1 reporting names the starting center or otherwise establishes the primary replacement role.

cases.reason: Houston placed Higgins on reserve/injured and subsequently traded for Kayshon Boutte, but current roster/reporting still supports a multi-receiver solution rather than a single verified Higgins replacement. Nico Collins, Boutte and other receivers remain active, while NFL reporting specifically describes multiple receivers filling the void.
cases.reopenTrigger: Current team/depth/coach reporting identifies one receiver as the primary role replacement for Higgins with sufficiently resolved alignment and usage.

cases.reason: San Francisco added Deebo Samuel after Pearsall's season-ending injury and expects Samuel to have a significant offensive role, but the current receiver room also includes Mike Evans, De'Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing. Current evidence does not establish a one-for-one Pearsall alignment/usage replacement.
cases.reopenTrigger: Official/reliable Week 1 role reporting establishes the primary receiver taking Pearsall's expected alignment and workload.

cases.reason: Atlanta continues to describe Walker as a multi-role force multiplier whose responsibilities span edge, off-ball, coverage and pressure roles. James Pearce Jr. is also unavailable to start the season, further preventing a defensible one-for-one replacement mapping.
cases.reopenTrigger: Atlanta establishes a stable Week 1 replacement/rotation map for Walker's major responsibilities sufficient to value the role without double-counting the Pearce absence.

cases.reason: Green Bay enters Week 1 with MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and newly acquired Kaleb Johnson while Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Team reporting has not named a single back who will absorb Jacobs' primary workload.
cases.reopenTrigger: Green Bay identifies a primary Jacobs replacement or a sufficiently defined workload split that can be role-weighted under the governed personnel system.

cases.reason: Mike Vrabel said September 1 that Gonzalez was not expected to practice that day and that the team first needs him back at practice before providing a game-status update. His Week 1 availability therefore remains unresolved despite his active-roster status.
cases.reopenTrigger: Practice participation and/or official Week 1 injury designation resolves Gonzalez's availability; if unavailable or materially limited, then resolve the outside-corner replacement assignment.

cases.reason: New Orleans placed Tyson on reserve/injured-designated for return. The public depth chart still lists Tyson and other unavailable players, so it is not reliable enough by itself to establish the Week 1 replacement role. Current roster reporting does not identify a one-for-one replacement.
cases.reopenTrigger: Current Week 1 team/coach reporting identifies Tyson's primary replacement alignment and expected usage after the final roster moves.

conclusion: All seven previously blocked Week 1 matchup cases were re-reviewed against current football information. None has enough resolved availability/replacement/role evidence to become numeric-eligible. Preserve all live Graham numbers and continue fail-closed monitoring.
